claims.text: Controlled alloying with a secondary metal will shift the d-band center of a transition-metal catalyst closer to the Fermi level.
Shifting the d-band center will tune the adsorption energies of reaction intermediates.
Tuning adsorption energies through a d-band-center shift will enhance catalytic activity.
Tuning adsorption energies through a d-band-center shift will improve catalytic selectivity.
Controlled alloying alters the catalyst's electronic density of states.
An optimal d-band-center shift improves adsorption-desorption dynamics.
Improved adsorption-desorption dynamics enhance reaction kinetics.
Catalysts whose d-band centers are shifted closer to the Fermi level will have higher turnover frequencies than unalloyed baseline catalysts.
Catalysts whose d-band centers are shifted closer to the Fermi level will have improved product selectivity relative to unalloyed baseline catalysts.
The d-band-center position relative to the Fermi level is measurable using XPS or UPS.
The comparison will hold temperature, pressure, reactant concentrations, catalyst morphology, and particle size constant.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when morphology, particle size, and support interactions are uniform and reaction conditions do not cause significant structural changes.
Alloying may cause structural changes that independently influence catalytic performance.
Failure of d-band-center changes to correlate with higher turnover frequency and selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.
